Test these items: constant 0..* parsing using the spec singular field name, constant.name 1..1 with sql-name validation and %name FHIRPath reference, value[x] 1..1 exactly-one behavior, primitive value types: base64Binary, boolean, canonical, code, date, dateTime, decimal, id, instant, integer, integer64, oid, string, positiveInt, time, unsignedInt, uri, url, uuid, constant substitution in column paths and where filters, invalid/missing constant values raise explicit spec errors. For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 ViewDefinition logical model: ViewDefinition.constant is 0..*, Constant.name is 1..1 sql-name, Constant.value[x] is 1..1; https://sql-on-fhir.org/ig/latest/StructureDefinition-ViewDefinition.html#ViewDefinition.constant
issues.evidence: Fresh probe .temp/qa/sof_vd02_skeptic_probe.py: parser accepted legacy top-level "constants" and created a ViewDefinition constant even though the logical model field is singular "constant". This can make invalid JSON appear valid and activate constant substitution under a non-spec field name.
issues.root_cause: Parser kept a legacy pre-spec alias for constants and treated it as equivalent to the official logical-model field.
issues.resolution: parse_view_definition now rejects the legacy plural constants field with an explicit ParseError; tests use the spec singular constant array.
issues.verified_in: .temp/qa/sof_vd02_skeptic_probe.py PASS; focused constants/parser/generator/where/DuckDB pytest 98 passed; ViewDefinition pytest 916 passed; ViewDefinition conformance 134/134; full conformance 2822/2822.

issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 ViewDefinition.constant.value[x] definition says constants are substituted through %your_constant_name in FHIRPath expressions; undefined constants are errors in official constant fixture; https://sql-on-fhir.org/ig/2.0.0/StructureDefinition-ViewDefinition-definitions.html#ViewDefinition.constant.value_x_
issues.evidence: Fresh direct API check: resolve_constants_in_path("gender = %Missing", {}) returned "gender = %Missing" with only a warning. Expected an explicit constant resolution error; generated SQL paths already reject undefined constants before execution.
issues.root_cause: The standalone constant resolver logged and preserved unknown external variables instead of sharing the generator error boundary.
issues.resolution: resolve_constants_in_path now raises ConstantResolutionError for undefined user constants while preserving built-in FHIRPath variables.

issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 ViewDefinition.constant.name is the FHIRPath external constant name used as %[name]; each external constant reference must resolve to one value; https://sql-on-fhir.org/ig/latest/StructureDefinition-ViewDefinition.html#ViewDefinition.constant.name
issues.evidence: Fresh direct check: parse_view_definition accepted two constants named "Dup". ConstantResolver.from_view_definition would silently keep the last value, making %Dup ambiguous instead of rejecting the duplicate definition.
issues.root_cause: Constant name uniqueness was only reported by the permissive warning API; strict parse and resolver paths did not enforce it.
issues.resolution: Parser and ConstantResolver construction now reject duplicate constant names instead of allowing last-wins resolution.

issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 ViewDefinition.constant.name has sql-name constraint and value[x] is exactly one of the supported primitive choice types; https://sql-on-fhir.org/ig/latest/StructureDefinition-ViewDefinition.html#ViewDefinition.constant
issues.evidence: Fresh direct checks: SQLGenerator accepted Constant(name="BadInteger", value="1", value_type="integer") and Constant(value_type="notatype") and emitted SQL; ViewDefinition.to_dict() serialized invalid constants including name "_bad" and integer value as a string. Parser rejects equivalent JSON, so direct dataclass and serializer boundaries are inconsistent.
issues.root_cause: Primitive constant validation lived in dict extraction, so direct Constant objects bypassed value_type/name/value shape checks.
issues.resolution: Added validate_constant_fields in types.py and reused it from Constant.to_dict and SQLGenerator._validate_constants for direct dataclass boundary parity.
